items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: Welk. Welk’s no longer. That’s about it.

ctx.x: Well Chuck Cecil runs programs, the hits of ’48 and ’49 and so on. And he always opens by talking about these dance halls and we all know where they were. There was the Palladium in L.A. where Goodman broke through. There was Glen Island Casino over here and Frank Daly’s Meadowbrook, and Boston, everyplace. There were places all over the country that were known because they were broadcast from there. And that’s how these bands were made. That’s how Goodman was made. Goodman was made because of the broadcasts on…
I think the Basie band is probably the truest to — at least they have a steady personnel. Some of the other ones come in and use local guys sometimes.
